text.content:
The Code of Milan is the Sabbat's closest equivalent to the Camarilla's Traditions - a sect-wide oath of conduct, sworn by the regent and consistory in the presence of all faction leaders, that every pack and faction is expected to honor or else openly declare separation from the sect. The current version was revised and re-sworn on December 21, 1933, in the aftermath of a destructive Sabbat civil war, and remains the standing code in the Final Nights.

The Statutes

  1. The Sabbat shall remain united in support of the regent; a new regent may be elected if necessary, and shall grant the sect freedom from tyranny.
  2. All Sabbat shall serve their leaders so long as those leaders serve the regent's will.
  3. All Sabbat shall faithfully observe the Auctoritas Ritae.
  4. All Sabbat shall keep their word of honor to one another.
  5. All Sabbat shall treat their peers fairly and equally, upholding the sect's strength and unity, and provide for the needs of their brethren when necessary.
  6. All Sabbat must put the good of the sect and the race of Cainites before their own personal needs, whatever the cost.
  7. Those who are not honorable under this code are considered less than equal and unworthy of assistance.
  8. The Lex Talionis (the principle of proportionate retaliation) is the model for justice all Sabbat must abide by.
  9. All Sabbat shall protect one another from the sect's enemies; personal enemies remain a personal responsibility unless they threaten sect security.
  10. All Sabbat shall protect Sabbat territory from all other powers.
  11. The spirit of freedom is the sect's fundamental principle; all Sabbat may expect and demand freedom from their leaders.
  12. The Ritus of Monomacy shall be used to settle disputes among all Sabbat.
  13. All Sabbat shall support the Black Hand.

Addenda (added the same night)

  1. All Sabbat have the right to monitor the behavior and activities of fellow sect members to maintain freedom and security.
  2. All Sabbat possess the right to call a council of their peers and immediate leaders.
  3. All Sabbat shall act against members who abuse the powers and authority the sect has given them for personal gain at the sect's expense - through accepted means only, approved by a quorum of prisci.

Factions that do not pledge themselves to the revised Code are considered to have claimed separation from the Sabbat - a status that carries serious consequences, since the Code's protections (and the duty of other Sabbat to come to a member's aid) no longer apply to them.
